description: How games generate levels, maps and challenges by algorithm and how they learn from the people who play them. Students build constructive, evolutionary and learned generators, measure their output, and fit player models that drive adaptive difficulty.
modelledOn: Shaker, Togelius and Nelson, Procedural Content Generation in Games
Yannakakis and Togelius, Artificial Intelligence and Games
Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (search and learning chapters)
Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning (clustering and generative model chapters)
outcomes: Implement constructive generators using noise, cellular automata, grammars, BSP trees and tile-constraint methods.
Formulate content generation as a search problem and build an evolutionary generator with a justified fitness function.
Train a simple machine-learned level generator and explain what its latent space and training data limit.
Evaluate a generator with expressive range analysis, playability checks and diversity metrics.
Build player models from telemetry using clustering, prediction and skill rating, and discuss their ethical limits.
Design an adaptive difficulty loop and a mixed-initiative design tool and test them against a stated player experience goal.

units.title: Constructive and grammar-based generation
topics: Taxonomy of generators: online versus offline, necessary versus optional content, controllability and determinism
Noise and terrain: value and gradient noise, fractal octaves and diamond-square
Cellular automata for caves and islands; smoothing rules and connectivity repair
Dungeon generation: BSP trees, rooms-and-corridors and graph-based layouts
L-systems and shape grammars for plants, buildings and quests
Markov chains and wave function collapse for tile-based levels

units.title: Search-based and evolutionary content generation
topics: Genetic algorithms: representation, selection, crossover and mutation for levels
Fitness functions: direct, simulation-based and interactive evaluation
Novelty search, quality diversity and MAP-Elites
Constraint solving and answer set programming for design rules
Multi-objective search: Pareto fronts and the NSGA-II algorithm

units.title: Machine-learned generators
topics: Learning from existing levels: encoding, training data and its limits
N-gram and recurrent models for sequences of tiles and rhythm
Autoencoders and generative adversarial networks; searching the latent space
Reinforcement learning as a level designer and large generative models for text and art assets
Data scarcity, copyright and bias in learned generators

units.title: Evaluating generators and expressive range
topics: Expressive range analysis: metrics such as linearity, leniency and density, and 2D histograms
Playability and solvability checks with simulated agents and path search
Diversity and novelty: edit distance, feature distance and repetition detection
Human evaluation: surveys, rankings and blind comparison of generated and hand-made content
Failure modes: degenerate content, bias towards simple outputs and confirmation of metrics

units.title: Player modelling and telemetry
topics: Player types and motivation taxonomies; model-based versus model-free approaches
Telemetry features and clustering players with k-means and hierarchical methods
Predicting churn, purchase and skill with logistic regression and decision trees
Skill rating systems: Elo-style updates, Glicko and matchmaking
Learning from play traces: behaviour cloning, procedural personas and privacy and ethics of modelling

units.title: Dynamic difficulty and experience-driven generation
topics: Flow theory: matching challenge to skill and the limits of the flow channel
Rule-based and model-based dynamic difficulty adjustment; rubber-banding
The experience-driven PCG loop: model the player, generate, evaluate, adapt
Affect and preference learning from ranked pairs
Bandits for content selection; fairness, manipulation and transparency in adaptation

units.title: Mixed-initiative design tools
topics: Co-creative design: suggestion, critique and variation in a designer's tool
Constraint-based editing and automatic repair of designer sketches
Interface design for control: sliders, examples and seeds
Evaluating tools with designers: task time, quality and creative ownership
Tools for small teams and low-resource studios; explainability of suggestions

units.title: Applications and project
topics: Generating quests, stories and dialogue with grammars and planning
Generating music, textures and shaders procedurally
Evaluating at scale: simulation, A/B tests and regression tests for generators
Case study: a mobile roguelike or puzzle game with generated levels and adaptive difficulty
Project: build, evaluate and report a generator coupled to a player model

schedule.title: Noise, caves and dungeons
schedule.exercise: Classify five well-known generators by the taxonomy, then generate a height map and a cave and explain what controls their roughness and connectivity.

tasks.title: Generate a 64 by 64 height map with value noise at four octaves and print the tile counts above and below sea level
Generate a cave with cellular automata for 5 smoothing passes and report the share of floor tiles in the largest connected region
Step through a cellular automata cave while varying the fill probability from 40 to 60 percent and find the value where connectivity collapses

schedule.title: Dungeons, grammars and tile constraints
schedule.exercise: Write an L-system for a branching baobab, a BSP rule for placing rooms and a set of tile adjacency rules for a village map.

tasks.title: Expand an L-system for five generations, print the string length at each generation and draw the result with turtle commands
Generate a BSP dungeon of 8 rooms joined by corridors and check with search that every room can be reached from the start
Run wave function collapse on a 12 by 12 grid with four tile types and record the contradictions and restarts across 20 seeds

schedule.title: Evolving content
schedule.exercise: Encode a platformer level as a vector of 40 gene values, define a fitness function that rewards a target difficulty, and explain what MAP-Elites adds over a plain genetic algorithm.

tasks.title: Watch a genetic algorithm evolve a bit string of 40 genes and plot best and average fitness per generation across 50 generations
Evolve a 20-room dungeon so that the shortest path from start to exit is near 30 steps, and report fitness over generations
Implement MAP-Elites over two behaviour axes for generated mazes and show the filled archive and the best maze in each cell

schedule.title: Generators learned from data
schedule.exercise: Train a tile-sequence model on ten levels, sample five new ones, and discuss what the training set bias and size do to the results.

tasks.title: Train a bigram model on tile columns from 10 hand-made levels and sample three new 40-column levels
Train a small autoencoder on 8 by 8 tile patches in the visualiser and inspect how reconstructions change with the latent size
Search the latent space of a trained autoencoder for patches that maximise a difficulty score and report the best five

schedule.title: Expressive range and playability
schedule.exercise: Compute linearity and leniency for 500 generated levels, plot their expressive range histogram, and test every level for solvability.

tasks.title: Plot a two-dimensional histogram of linearity against leniency for 300 supplied level metrics and describe the empty regions
Use A* to test whether 30 generated mazes are solvable and report the share failing and the nodes expanded on average
Compute pairwise edit distances for 200 generated levels, flag near-duplicates under a threshold and report the generator's diversity score

schedule.title: Human evaluation and failure modes
schedule.exercise: Design a blind comparison of generated and hand-made levels with 12 players, state the hypothesis, and list three ways a generator can score well on metrics while being dull to play.

tasks.title: Compute mean ranking of generated and hand-made levels from a table of 15 players and chart the two groups
Test whether players prefer generated levels over hand-made ones with a binomial test on 40 pairwise choices and state the conclusion
Find the degenerate outputs of a given generator by sampling 1,000 levels and design a repair or reject rule that removes them

schedule.title: Modelling players from telemetry
schedule.exercise: Cluster 300 player sessions into three groups using five features, name each group from its feature means, and predict churn with a simple classifier.

tasks.title: Cluster 100 player sessions into 3 groups with k-means on two features and plot the clusters with their centres
Cluster 300 sessions using 5 telemetry features with k-means, pick k with the silhouette score and name the player groups
Train a logistic regression and a decision tree to predict churn after 3 sessions, and compare precision and recall on a held-out set

schedule.title: Skill, traces and ethics of modelling
schedule.exercise: Update Elo-style ratings for a ten-game tournament, then outline how play traces could be used to build a persona and what must be protected.

tasks.title: Update Elo ratings for 6 players over 20 matches and print the table and the rating gap that predicted each upset
Build a matchmaking function that pairs 50 rated players to keep predicted win probability between 40 and 60 percent and check its fairness
Clone a player's moves in a small maze game by supervised learning on recorded traces and compare its path lengths with the original player

schedule.title: Flow and dynamic difficulty adjustment
schedule.exercise: Design a rule-based difficulty controller for an endless runner and describe how it changes when a learned player model supplies its input.

tasks.title: Plot challenge against skill on the flow diagram for six player traces and mark when each one is bored or anxious
Implement a rule-based difficulty adjuster for an endless runner and show it keeps simulated players near a 60 percent success rate
Close the loop: a player model estimates skill, a generator makes a level at that difficulty, and 200 simulated players test the result

schedule.title: Preference learning and adaptive content
schedule.exercise: Learn a preference score from 30 ranked pairs of levels, and discuss when adaptive difficulty crosses into manipulation of the player.

tasks.title: Fit a linear preference score to 30 ranked pairs of levels and report the accuracy on 10 held-out pairs
Implement an epsilon-greedy bandit choosing among 4 level styles and measure regret over 1,000 simulated players
Compare epsilon-greedy and Thompson sampling for content selection when player taste drifts, and report cumulative reward for both

schedule.title: Tools that work with designers
schedule.exercise: Sketch a mixed-initiative level editor that proposes three completions of a half-drawn level, with controls for the designer, and plan how to test it with five designers.

tasks.title: Produce three variations of a designer's half-finished level by random fills that keep their fixed tiles unchanged
Write a repair function that fixes unreachable rooms in a designer's sketch with the fewest tile edits, and report the edits made
Analyse a study of 8 designers using the tool versus not, comparing completion time and quality scores with a paired test

schedule.title: Narrative, audio and scalable testing
schedule.exercise: Generate a quest with a grammar, list the checks you would automate for a generator in a nightly build, and design an A/B test for a new difficulty rule.

tasks.title: Generate 10 fetch-and-deliver quests from a grammar and check each one has a giver, an item, a place and a reward
Write a regression test that runs a generator on 500 seeds and fails when solvability or diversity drops below set thresholds
Size an A/B test of two difficulty rules for retention by computing the sample needed to detect a 3 point difference at 80 percent power

schedule.title: Project: generator plus player model
schedule.exercise: Present your generator, its evaluation plots and the player model that drives it, with a limitations section on bias, repetition and fairness.

tasks.title: Run the case study roguelike generator for 100 seeds and tabulate level size, solvability and enemy count
Plot the expressive range of your project generator before and after adding the player model and describe the change
Run 500 simulated players through your generator with adaptive difficulty on and off and report retention-like measures and fairness across skill groups
